title: 31st Sitting of first Session of 2025
summary: The sitting opened at 09:01 with 38 members present, accepted the minutes of the 25th to 27th sittings and took a long question session with the Minister of Agriculture and Animal Welfare on cat shelters, farmland, island leasing, imports, pesticides and farmer training. A government bill amending the Aviation Authority Act had its first reading announced. Members then debated Judiciary Committee reports: the Bandaara Naaib's Office Bill, where debate closed with the vote left for voting time, and the committee's report on the removal of Supreme Court judge Dr. Azmiralda Zahir, which drew sharp exchanges, several points of order and a break from 10:30 to 11:00. The report on a second Supreme Court judge, Mahaz Ali Zahir, was presented and debate had just begun when this part ends. Debate continued on the Judiciary Committee's reports on removing two Supreme Court judges, Dr. Azmiralda Zahir and Al-Ustaaz Mahaz Ali Zahir, after the Judicial Service Commission referred their cases. Supporters said the Commission and the committee followed the law and that earlier governments removed judges too, while opponents said the process was politically driven and tied to the question of MPs losing their seats. At vote time members rejected passing the Vice President's Office Bill as the committee had decided (3 yes, 67 no), then sent it back to the committee, and voted 68 to 11 to remove each of the two judges. The sitting was adjourned to Thursday 15 May 2025. Parts of the text layer are jumbled, so some speaker gists are approximate.

speakers.name: Dr. Mariyam Mariya
positions: As Minister of Agriculture and Animal Welfare, answered questions on cat shelter running costs, farmland, island leasing, imports, chemicals and training programmes.
Said an MOU deadline for the cat facility was missed, with the ministry working to complete outstanding requirements.
Said agro training would be widened to all atolls and a smart agriculture and farmer-loan route was being explored.

speakers.name: Hassan Zareer
positions: Asked about reviving farming on Ferodhoo and Maalhos and what plans exist to make agriculture an income source.
On the Azmiralda Zahir report, supported it and argued the JSC had followed its procedures.
Argued earlier governments also influenced the courts and cited a past court case as an example, with repeated chair interventions.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Nazil
positions: Asked when roughly 250 idle Agro National staff will be given work and how foreign workers in farming are monitored.
On the Azmiralda Zahir report, said the committee gave the judge no chance to respond and criticised how the committee was run.
Asked the Majlis to send the report back to the Judiciary Committee, citing JSC Act provisions on how a complaint should be handled.

speakers.name: Abdul Gafoor Moosa
positions: Described the judge as exemplary and said the question raised was about integrity and honesty.
Argued the government was removing people it dislikes and pointed to corruption, rights and credit-rating concerns.
Called the day a dark one in the country's history and said the government was weakening the Supreme Court to serve its aims.
Described the two judges as among the most upright on the bench and said removing them was not the right course.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Shujau
positions: Asked whether MDP members have met the minister about constituency issues and whether the minister is available to them.
On the Bandaara Naaib's Office Bill, supported the committee report, saying earlier governments also sought a separate office.
Said opposition members objected without having read the bill, and that the bill aims to attract capable lawyers.
Strongly backed the two Judiciary Committee reports on removing the Supreme Court judges.

speakers.name: Ahmed Azaan Marzooq
positions: Asked when practical work will start on the China-backed agriculture project signed last year at Fushi Dhiggaru.
On the Azmiralda Zahir report, raised concerns about the JSC's procedures and its decision not to accept some defence evidence.
Called for the committee to let the judges respond before the Majlis decides, citing statements by international bodies and the Human Rights Commission.

speakers.name: Hussain Ziyad
positions: Invited the minister to Vaikaradhoo and asked for accurate information on greenhouses under the IFAD project and any bank loan requirement.
Opposed the reports, arguing they are driven by concern over a possible Supreme Court ruling on MPs losing their seats.
Said the majority could pursue its aim by amending the Constitution, and urged members not to use Parliament's power this way.
Warned that the same power could later be turned on members of the current majority.

speakers.name: Husnee Mubarik
positions: As Judiciary Committee chair, presented the reports on the Bandaara Naaib's Office Bill and on the two Supreme Court judges.
Said the committee found the JSC followed procedure and has no power to investigate judges, and that the Counsel General's advice did not change its view.
Raised a point of order that a speaker's claims about the committee's process went against the Rules of Procedure.

speakers.name: Abdul Sattar Mohamed
positions: Supported the Azmiralda Zahir report, saying the committee acted within the rules and law.
Argued the committee had no duty to summon the judge and criticised how earlier governments treated judges.

speakers.name: Hussain Riza Adam
positions: Argued the Attorney General's advice misreads the Judicial Service Commission Act and that the Commission acted within the powers the Act gives it.
Cited past cases and court rulings to argue the process followed matched established practice.
Said that even if a procedural flaw existed, it did not harm the rights of the two judges.

speakers.name: Ahmed Thariq
positions: Said the dispute stems from how the Judicial Service Commission's composition is set by the parliamentary majority, and defended the current set-up.
Rejected the claim that suspending two judges halts the Supreme Court, saying full-bench cases are limited and vacancies can arise.
Criticised opposition figures for seeking foreign help over the judiciary and recalled earlier judge removals.

speakers.name: Ameen Faisal
positions: Asked whether imports that undercut local produce, especially in Ramadan, can be controlled and how many farmers have been trained.
Opposed the reports, saying the public gave the majority its power to be used lawfully, and regretted the Speaker's part in the Commission's decision.
Said giving the judges a chance to respond would not change the outcome given the majority, and warned the same power could later be used against today's majority.

speakers.name: Ismail Nizar
positions: As a committee member, said the report explains the JSC's powers under section 22 of its Act and supports the committee's findings.
Rejected the opposition view that the case began incorrectly.

speakers.name: Mohamed Ibrahim
positions: Asked why the cat shelter opened in November 2024 has housed no cats and whether staff and supplies are in place.
Asked for the shelter's daily running cost, including cost per cat.

speakers.name: Mohamed Niushad
positions: Asked how many cats are under the ministry's care, how many political appointees it has, and what procedure is used to lease islands.
Raised a point of order that the Baarashu member's remarks were not about the report before the House.

speakers.name: Dr. Ahmed Shamheed
positions: Said the bill does not fix pay or lawyer recruitment, lets the office set its own structure and sets retirement at 55 with benefits.
Said a separate law is not the right fix and not common practice elsewhere; in a point of order disputed a Singapore comparison.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Hussain
positions: Asked whether Fuvahmulah farmers' land problem can be solved, when, and when easier opportunities for farmers will be created.

speakers.name: Ahmed Didi
positions: Asked how the minister would protect a distinctive bird in Addu that is being preyed on, suggesting removal of the predator.

speakers.name: Saudulla Hilmy
positions: Asked when uninhabited islands in Huvadhu atoll will be leased, saying they are being damaged and could bring the state income.

speakers.name: Ahmed Shakir
positions: Asked how many farm visits the ministry made in 2024 and 2025 and how chemical pesticides and their after-effects are regulated.

speakers.name: Hussain Sameer
positions: Asked what help farmers get after heavy rain damage, whether chemical limits and testing exist, and if Thoddoo has a modern farming plan.

speakers.name: Abdulla Shareef
positions: Asked how betel leaf farming in Kela and Filladhoo can be revived, citing falling output, market stocking and ferry supply limits.

speakers.name: Ahmed Riyaz
positions: Asked what plans the government has for agriculture in Thaa atoll, saying earlier governments did little there.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Falah
positions: Supported the Bandaara Naaib's Office Bill report, noting the bill passed first reading with all members' agreement and meets a clear need.

speakers.name: Mohamed Abbas
positions: Supported the bill, saying it would speed up the Majlis's legal work and let the office handle its internal difficulties.

speakers.name: Mohamed Shahid
positions: Raised a point of order reminding members of their oath and asking what members had said in the 18th and 19th Majlis.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Didi
positions: Supported the report on judge Mahaz Ali Zahir, saying the committee followed the law and earlier practice, and referred to the 18th and 19th Majlis.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Muhammad
positions: Fully supported the reports and urged that they pass quickly, framing the question as one of justice.
Cited a 2011 sitting record and the 2019 removal of Supreme Court judges to criticise the MDP's record on justice.

speakers.name: Abdul Rahman
positions: Opposed the reports, saying he believed the decision was reached under outside influence and not on the merits.
Noted the Attorney General's view that the Commission did not complete the legal procedures when taking up the two judges' cases.

decisions: Minutes of the 25th to 27th sittings were accepted after no amendments were proposed.
First reading of the Aviation Authority Act (Law 2/2012) amendment bill was announced.
Debate on the Bandaara Naaib's Office Bill report closed; vote to be asked at voting time.
Debate on the Dr. Azmiralda Zahir report closed; vote to be asked at voting time.
Passing the Vice President's Office Bill as decided in the Judiciary Committee's report was not approved (3 yes, 67 no).
The Vice President's Office Bill was sent back to the Judiciary Committee for further work (70 yes, 0 no, 2 abstain).
Supreme Court judge Dr. Azmiralda Zahir was removed from office (68 yes, 11 no).
Supreme Court judge Al-Ustaaz Mahaz Ali Zahir was removed from office (68 yes, 11 no).
The Speaker adjourned the House to the next sitting on Thursday 15 May 2025 at 09:00.
